correctness.rationale: In a real Gram factorization A=BB^T with B^TB diagonal, the residual trace is T minus the Rayleigh quotient of B^TB in the chosen row direction, where T=lambda1+lambda2. With t the squared fraction of a nonzero row in the second eigendirection, that gives R=lambda2+(lambda1−lambda2)t. Weighting the rows by squared norm/T gives E[t]=lambda2/T, hence exactly the stated mean. Conversely two rows of norm squared w_j T/2 with second-coordinate fractions t_j and opposite signs of the second coordinate give diagonal covariance contributions w_j T(1−t_j,t_j), without off-diagonal terms. Summing gives the two strictly positive eigenvalues and ensures the two pivots associated to atom j have the prescribed total mass w_j; the endpoint and one-atom cases need no exceptions. Jensen and the secant bound yield attainable convex-order and variance extremes; for m<u<=lambda1 the inequality R−lambda2 >= (u−lambda2)1_{R>=u} is exact on the two-point witness supported at lambda2 and u. The deterministic law handles u=m and lower, and the interval support handles u>lambda1. No fixed-dimension claim is needed.
residual_risks: This analytic check covers exactly one pivot and varying dimension; no formal/external attestation. The recorded three-atom trials sample the endpoint-plus-center pattern and are not a substitute for the paired-row proof.

originality.rationale: Do not credit the pivot rule, the mean, or a new general convex risk inequality. The supported distinct content is the exact inverse statement: every finite scalar law with the specified interval and mean is attained by real rank-two inputs of the specified spectrum, and the worst-case intermediate tail is attained within that class. The inspected work gives expectations, convex estimates, or different input/sampling restrictions, not this realizability and sharpness.
residual_risks: A prior equivalent decomposition theorem in frame, moment or ensemble theory may exist; the general frame-completion source named above was not read. No historical-priority guarantee follows from the bounded checks.

value.rationale: A spectrum-only expectation does not quantify the reliability of the randomized numerical step. The converse resolves whether that information can be strengthened to a finer universal distributional constraint: in this base case there is none except finite support, the interval, and the mean. In particular, exact attainable probability at any threshold and actual equal-spectrum witnesses show why the first moment cannot certify typical behavior. The elementary bounds by themselves would not be the contribution.
residual_risks: The result gives worst-case as opposed to typical-input information, and variable-dimension rank-two sharpness is not a general high-rank or multistep confidence theorem.
